title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease
title_zh: 单细胞和空间转录组学中的细胞异质性阿尔茨海默病研究
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined neuropathologically by the presence of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, yet these canonical lesions alone cannot account for its clinical, regional and cellular heterogeneity. AD is a multicellular, spatially organized disease shaped by the interactions of neurons, glia and vascular cells within distinct anatomical microenvironments. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have made it possible to dissect the transcriptional signatures of individual cell populations in the AD brain, revealing selective neuronal vulnerability, stage-dependent glial remodelling and widespread disruption of cell–cell communication networks, whereas spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging have anchored these molecular changes to their tissue context. Studies of defined populations, such as people with autosomal-dominant AD or Down syndrome-associated AD, and of the oldest-old cohorts help disentangle the molecular changes that are causal drivers from those that are downstream consequences. Across individuals, AD heterogeneity is further shaped by sex and ancestry, underscoring the need for broader representation of these factors in single-cell and spatial studies. These advances are also reshaping translational pipelines through multi-omic benchmarking of animal models and single-cell-based drug-repurposing strategies. Thus, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are redefining our understanding of AD heterogeneity and informing precision approaches to treatment. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing technologies have advanced our understanding of the molecular responses of specific cellular populations to Alzheimer disease (AD). Swarup and colleagues outline the insights that these approaches have provided into the multicellular interactions that underlie AD pathogenesis and heterogeneity.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）在病理上以淀粉样斑块和神经纤维样缠结为特征，然而这些典型病变单独无法解释其临床、区域和细胞层面的异质性。AD是一种多细胞、空间组织的疾病，由神经元、胶质细胞和血管细胞在不同解剖微环境中的相互作用塑造。单细胞和单核RNA测序技术使得能够解析AD大脑中个体细胞群体的转录特征，揭示了选择性神经元脆弱性、随阶段变化的胶质重塑以及广泛的细胞间通讯网络破坏；而空间转录组学和多重成像则将这些分子变化锚定于组织语境。研究自变异性AD或唐氏综合征相关AD的人群，以及最老年人群体，有助于区分致病性分子变化与继发性变化。在个体间，AD异质性进一步受性别和种族的影响，这凸显了在单细胞和空间研究中需要更广泛地代表这些因素。这些进展也正在通过动物模型的多组学基准测定和基于单细胞的药物再利用策略重塑转化流程。因此，单细胞和空间转录组学正在重新定义我们对AD异质性的理解，并指向精准的治疗方法。单细胞和单核RNA测序技术已推进我们对特定细胞群体对阿尔茨海默病（AD）分子响应的理解。Swarup及其同事概述了这些方法在阐释AD病理基础和异质性背后多细胞相互作用所提供的见解。
